title: Property Descriptions
description: Natural-language guidance attached to individual parameters and nested properties.
question: Do property-level descriptions survive at each capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP tools documenting individual parameters.
known_issues: A retained type without its property description can still leave a model unable to choose the intended value.
why: Property descriptions carry the author's parameter-level intent. Losing them can make a structurally valid tool call semantically wrong.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: descriptions on the URI and object branches of destination.anyOf are absent from the generated args_schema.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Property descriptions survive at the top level, but descriptions on the branches of an `anyOf` are dropped.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`. The descriptions on both `destination.anyOf` branches and on the `create_report.config` object are absent from the generated schema; the other descriptions survive, with allowed values and ranges appended to them.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: the four tools that reach the model keep their property descriptions. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its four property descriptions never reach the model.
